title: Artin tensor acyclicity for strict-local algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $B_1,B_2$ be ind-etale $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Assume that each $\operatorname{Spec}(B_j)$ is etale acyclic, meaning every etale covering of it splits (equivalently, every connected component is strictly henselian). Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}(B_1\otimes_R B_2)$. Then for every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], one has $H^q(T_{\mathrm{Et}},F)=0$ for every $q>0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: Hübner–Schmidt, Definition 7.8, Proposition 7.9 (étale case, after Artin, On the joins of Hensel rings, Proposition 3.2) and Theorem 7.10 (étale case), printed pp. 14–15. The passage from étale acyclicity to vanishing cohomology: since every étale covering of the affine scheme $T$ splits, $\Gamma(T,-)$ is exact on abelian sheaves, so its higher derived functors vanish, as in the last sentence of the proof of Stacks Project etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03QO.
